title: X Education Lead Scoring Model
tagline: Logistic-regression lead scoring (0–100) to lift an online-education sales team off a ~30% conversion rate: AUC 0.97, and 92% of flagged 'hot' leads converted.
summary: A lead scoring model for X Education, an online course platform whose leads converted at only about 30% against a CEO target of 80%. A 12-variable logistic regression scores ~9,000 leads from 0 to 100 (AUC 0.97, ~92% accuracy on held-out data), so the sales team can focus calls on the leads most likely to buy.
role: Analyst and modeler: data cleaning, EDA, feature selection, model building and evaluation, the sales playbooks, and the stakeholder deck and executive summary.

caseStudy.problem: X Education generated plenty of leads but converted only about 30% of them. The CEO's target was 80%. Without any way to rank leads, the sales team spent equal time on every lead, most of whom would never buy.

stakeholders.role: Set the 80% conversion target and was the audience for the executive summary and recommendations.
Primary users of the 0–100 lead scores, using them to decide who to call first and who to move to email nurturing.
Given an 'aggressive mode' call list for the two-month intern period, when the goal is to reach as many likely converters as possible.
Given recommendations on website engagement, SMS outreach and targeting management specializations.

approach: Cleaned ~9,000 leads across 37 fields: dropped columns over 40% empty or filled in by sales only after a call, added an 'Others' category instead of losing the 37% of leads with no specialization, and standardized inconsistent labels.
EDA found that time spent on the website was the strongest behavioral signal (r = 0.36 with conversion) and that visits and page views overlapped heavily (r = 0.77).
Dummy-encoded the data to 81 features, used RFE to narrow it to 20, then refined over 9 GLM iterations, dropping variables with high p-values and VIF scores above 5.
Settled on a 12-variable logistic regression, chose a 0.38 probability cutoff from the sensitivity/specificity trade-off, and turned probabilities into 0–100 lead scores.
Turned the model's coefficients into two sales playbooks: one for intern season and one for quarters when the target is already met.
caseStudy.solution: A lead scoring pipeline that gives every lead a 0–100 conversion score, plus a stakeholder deck, an executive summary and scenario playbooks that tell the sales team who to call, who to email and who to skip.

impactMetrics.label: AUC-ROC
impactMetrics.description: near-perfect separation of converters from non-converters

impactMetrics.label: Hot-lead precision
impactMetrics.description: of leads the model flags as likely to convert, about 92% did (training set)

impactMetrics.label: Held-out accuracy
impactMetrics.description: with 96% sensitivity on the test set, so the model generalizes rather than overfits

impactMetrics.label: Baseline → target
impactMetrics.description: the conversion gap the scoring model was built to close

businessOutcome: Showed a path to the CEO's 80% target: leads the model flags as likely to convert did convert about 92% of the time historically, compared with a ~30% baseline across all leads.

Gave sales a 'conservation mode' for quarters when the target is met early: call only leads scoring 80 or more, move mid-tier leads to automated email, and drop leads tagged 'Ringing', 'Might be' or 'Worst' to cut wasted calls.

Gave the intern season an 'aggressive mode' call list prioritizing working professionals, highly engaged website visitors, SMS-responsive leads and management specializations, plus time-limited sign-up incentives.
Pointed marketing to the strongest signals of intent: website engagement, form fills (Lead Add Form) and SMS activity.
caseStudy.learnings: Keeping the model interpretable was the point. A 12-variable logistic regression with readable coefficients gave the sales team rules they could act on, like 'call working professionals who got an SMS', not just a score they had to take on faith.
